Cloud machines (boat.dev) · optional
  When every machine of yours is at its agent limit, work runs on a few sleeping boat.dev machines of your own account, within budgets you set.
<QR>
  1. Make a boat.dev organization with one seat
     It costs the same as a personal plan, and its owner can cap their own seat, so boat.dev itself stops everything at your cap whatever fleetd does. Leave auto top-up and extra starts off: past the plan, starts are refused rather than billed.
     boat.dev: https://boat.dev
     Seats and limits: https://docs.boat.dev/organizations/seats-and-limits
     Control your spend: https://docs.boat.dev/billing#control-your-spend
     Plan: $20 a month: it includes $20 of machine time and 200 starts a day
     Billing › Auto top-up: Off
     Billing › Extra starts on invoice: Off
     Members › you › Machine time cap:
       300 hours a month
       Recommended: boat.dev stops your machines within a minute of it.
     Members › you › Machines at once:
       3
       Your pool size: 3 unless you change it below.
<QR>
  2. Make an environment for fleetd
     Cloud machines are made in it, with none of your account's secrets, AI logins or in-machine boat.dev key.
     Environments: https://docs.boat.dev/environments
     Name:
       fleetd-hub
     Safe for third parties: On
<QR>
  3. Make the hub's API key
     Only what the hub needs to make, wake, stop and delete its machines, and ssh for its tunnel: the hub dials each machine it wakes and holds an SSH tunnel its node reaches the hub through, so the hub needs no public address. No exec, file or snapshot actions: the hub never runs anything on a cloud machine.
     API key scopes: https://docs.boat.dev/api-keys/scopes
     Name:
       fleetd-hub
     Actions:
       sandbox.create sandbox.read sandbox.update sandbox.stop sandbox.resume sandbox.delete ssh account.read
       Not the presets: ci and admin give far more.
     Scope: environment:
       fleetd-hub
     Expires: 365 days
<QR>
  4. Choose the pool, the budgets and the projects
     Paste the key, Test it, then pick these and turn cloud machines on. Before you do, fleetd shows the most the pool can cost a day and a typical day. Work goes to a cloud machine only when every machine of yours is at its agent limit.
     boat.dev environment:
       fleetd-hub
       The one you made in part 2: machines are made in it, where the key reaches.
     Machines: 3 × large (8 vCPUs, 16 GB, $0.072 an hour each)
     Day budget: $3
     Month budget: your plan's included dollars ($20)
     Projects: the ones you tick: their code, transcripts and the secrets sealed there go to boat.dev
<QR>
  Cloud machines run on boat.dev: boat.dev can see what runs on them, as any host can. Paste the key, set the pool and turn it on in Settings › Hub › Machines › Cloud machines.
<QR>
  Test: Ask boat.dev what the key may read, then wake (or make) a cloud machine and check the hub's tunnel to it and its node's hello.
–  Cloud machines (boat.dev) optional · fleetd init --step cloud

Run fleetd init --step cloud again when you've done it; it keeps what's done.
